summary.headline: GRP Q1 FY27: EBITDA rose 60% to INR174 million, margin up 233 bps to 11%, with consolidated total income up 26% to INR1,573 million.
summary.overview: Consolidated total income grew 26% YoY to INR1,573 million, driven by Pyrova Energy utilisation, reclaim rubber volumes and better realisations in domestic and export markets. EBITDA rose 60% to INR174 million and PAT more than doubled to INR42 million despite sharp raw material inflation. Management re-segmented the business into Rubber Recycling and Others, and for the first time gave FY27 outlook: close to 20%+ revenue growth and continued margin improvement. Polymer composite was permanently shut due to US tariffs, while indirect export volumes to non-US countries are not yet fully recovered.

financial_highlights.change: Gross margin moderated on higher raw material costs (about 180 bps decline per analyst question)
More than doubled YoY, after prior period items
vs INR46 million in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Rubber Recycling (Reclaim Rubber, Custom Die Forms, Pyrova Energy)
segments.commentary: Standalone segment revenue grew 34% YoY; reclaim volumes +12% and reclaim export volumes +20%. Segment margins expanded on better realisations and manufacturing efficiency despite elevated raw material and logistics costs.

segments.name: Others (Engineering Plastics, Windmill, residual Polymer composite)
segments.commentary: Revenue broadly stable against a higher base that included polymer composite, now permanently shut. Engineering plastics volumes +27%; plastic verticals EBITDA margin up 14 pp YoY on a 10-pt gross margin improvement.

segments.name: Pyrova Energy (within Rubber Recycling)
segments.commentary: Cumulative investment about INR91 crore. Longest continuous reactor run achieved; July 2026 hit a 25-day monthly run with 4-day shutdown benchmark. Still sub-scale to standalone profitability (margin in single digits during ramp-up).

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth close to 20%+, driven by Pyrova, reclaim capacity growth and plastics; double-digit volume growth targeted for reclaim.
Reclaim Rubber FY27 volume growth close to 20%; medium term mid-teen volume growth and double-digit revenue growth over next 3 years; EBITDA margin from ~9-10% average to 10-14%.
Pyrova capacity to 45,000 tons after two more pyrolysis lines, then a further 30,000 tons in FY28; Pyrova EBITDA margin to 18-20% (management also cited 15-20% standalone) once rCB is mature.
Plastics (nylon and polyolefin): over 20% growth this fiscal, then mid-teen growth through FY30; EBITDA margin 10-15% (later stated 12-15% for plastics business).

FY27 capex targeted at INR90-100 crore (Pyrova lines, rCB plant, reclaim debottlenecking); FY28 capex decision in 2H FY27 subject to Solapur facility outcome; about INR100 crore left to reach INR250 crore expansion target.
capex_capacity: Pyrova first phase commissioned October 2025, stabilised by March 2026; two more pyrolysis lines to take capacity to 45 KTA.
rCB plant commissioning to start August 2026 and be completed by October 2026; meaningful contribution expected by Q4 FY27.
Target of an additional 30,000 tons pyrolysis and 12,000 tons rCB capacity in Gujarat over time.
Reclaim rubber debottlenecking and new technologies planned to add capacity.
Pyrova expected to generate INR250-300 crore revenue from the investment at 15-20% standalone EBITDA margin (per management).
demand_pricing: Reclaim export volumes +20% YoY, mainly North America recovery post US tariff easing; early growth from Europe and other markets.
Domestic reclaim market share up about 1% YoY; export share stable in India, up in targeted geographies.
Polymer composite permanently shut due to tariffs; non-US indirect export volumes not yet recovered.
Overall revenue growth ~30% of which ~12% volume and balance price; most raw-material cost pass-through achieved but contracts (quarterly, 6-monthly, annual) cause lag.
Reclaim being viewed as a strong alternative to virgin synthetic rubber amid oil-linked price volatility; customer buying framed on value, not just price.
Nylon growth driven by automotive OE demand; some appliance approvals converted to volumes in Q1. Polyolefin volumes flat as management is selective on customers.

qa_highlights.question: Has the tariff disruption permanently changed competition, and has GRP won customers from global peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Polymer composite shutdown is a permanent loss to revenue and margin; reclaim and custom die forms volumes are back to pre-tariff levels with a positive currency-driven margin effect versus pre-February 2026. Indirect non-US export volumes not yet recovered.

qa_highlights.question: Will rubber inflation persist, and how much has prices risen?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to forecast rubber prices, citing El Nino effects on natural rubber and oil-linked synthetic rubber. Most raw-material pass-through achieved, with a lag due to contract terms; expects double-digit volume growth for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 and FY28 capex and deleveraging plan?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex INR90-100 crore. FY28 capex to be decided in 2H FY27. About INR100 crore of the INR250 crore plan remains. Deleveraging timing not in management's control; no firm plans yet, though cash generation is expected.

qa_highlights.question: Update on rCB trials, expected revenue and margins; drivers of 27% engineering plastics volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: rCB plant commissioning from next month, completion by October 2026; expects contribution from Q4 FY27. Pyrova margin of 18-20% depends on customer approvals; FY28 seen as maturity year. Plastics growth mainly automotive OE, with some appliance approvals starting in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Customer conversations: are buyers moving to sustainability-led solutions rather than price?
qa_highlights.answer: Both factors; positioning is on value (mechanical/chemical properties, end-of-life compliance, cost versus virgin). Reclaim seen as an alternative as virgin rubber and carbon black prices are volatile; plastics adoption driven by regulation and cost.

qa_highlights.question: Export recovery vs share gains, structural margin drivers, Pyrova utilisation and EBITDA-positive timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Export volumes +20%, mainly North America recovery plus Europe base. Pyrova hit a 25-day monthly run in July 2026. Next milestones: rCB commissioning (Oct 2026), rCB product quality, tire-industry approval, then template replication 6-8 months after rCB commissioning. No firm EBITDA-positive date given.

risks_watch: Pyrova ramp-up risk: margin is in single digits today and the 18-20% target depends on rCB commissioning (October 2026), customer approvals and reactor utilisation; management said FY28 is when maturity is expected.
rCB product qualification: management said it will take several quarters after commissioning before a product is approved by the tire industry, so near-term rCB revenue contribution is uncertain.
Raw material pass-through lag: gross margin moderated on rubber inflation; contracts reset quarterly, six-monthly or annually, and management declined to forecast rubber prices.
Indirect non-US export volumes are not yet recovered; polymer composite is permanently shut, so the revenue and margin loss from it is permanent.
Capex and leverage: FY27 capex of INR90-100 crore and an FY28 decision in 2H FY27 depend on the Solapur outcome; management gave no firm deleveraging plan.
Plastics volume quality: polyolefin volumes were flat, nylon growth came mainly from automotive OE, and management said it is unclear whether this growth will repeat.
key_quotes: So, all of this should help us deliver a significantly higher revenue growth.
I do believe that this margin that we have generated in Q1 is not a onetime margin generation.
The threshold in the industry from a performance perspective is for a run of minimum of 25 days in a month and a 4 -day shutdown on the pyrolysis.
So, at this stage, it may be a little premature to put out an announcement of the likely numbers.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and the Pyrova operating milestones, and it gave the first FY27 outlook. It was cautious and non-committal on rubber price direction, gross margin, Pyrova EBITDA timing, FY28 capex and deleveraging, saying these depend on contracts, customer approvals or future decisions.
